result.stdout:
Usage: dotnet runic dev [application-arguments...] [options]

Run the application with development watchers.

Arguments:
  application-arguments  Arguments after -- are passed to the application.

Options:
  --no-restore             Skip the .NET restore and the JavaScript package install. The build does
                           not install missing frontend packages either.
  --no-frontend-watch      Build the frontend once instead of starting its development server or
                           watcher.
  --no-dotnet-watch        Run the application once instead of restarting it under dotnet watch
                           after C# edits.
  --dry-run                Print the evaluated project configuration and exit without changing files
                           or starting processes.
  --project, -p <project>  The project file, or a directory with one .csproj. Defaults to the
                           current directory.
  --configuration, -c <configuration>
                           The build configuration. [default: Debug]
  -h, --help               Show help
  --version                Show version
  --output <human|json>    Select output format

Examples:
  dotnet runic dev
  dotnet runic dev --project ./MyApp.csproj -- --app-argument

result.stdout:
Usage: dotnet runic doctor [options]

Check the project and development environment.

Options:
  --aot                       With --rid, check a publish with -p:PublishAot=true.
  --self-contained            With --rid, check a publish with --self-contained true.
  --project, -p <project>     The project file, or a directory with one .csproj. Defaults to the
                              current directory.
  --configuration, -c <configuration>
                              The build configuration to evaluate. Defaults to Debug, or Release
                              with --rid as dotnet publish does.
  --fail-on <fail-on>         Fail when a check reaches this status: never, fail or warn. Defaults
                              to fail for human output and never for JSON output.
  --rid, --runtime, -r <rid>  Also check deployment prerequisites for this runtime identifier, for
                              example linux-x64, win-x64 or osx-arm64.
  -h, --help                  Show help
  --version                   Show version
  --output <human|json>       Select output format

Examples:
  dotnet runic doctor --project ./MyApp.csproj
  dotnet runic doctor --rid linux-x64 --aot
  dotnet runic doctor --output json

result.stdout:
Usage: dotnet runic size [options]

Measure a published application and write a size report.

Options:
  --no-aot                 Publish without Native AOT.
  --verify-argument <verify-arguments...>
                           An argument for the --verify executable. Repeat it for several arguments.
  --project, -p <project>  The project file, or a directory with one .csproj. Defaults to the
                           current directory.
  --runtime, -r <runtime>  The runtime identifier to publish for, for example linux-x64. Required.
  --configuration, -c <configuration>
                           The build configuration. [default: Release]
  --report <report>        The JSON report to write. The file must not exist yet.
                           [default: runic-size.json]
  --verify <verify>        An executable to run after a successful publish, as a path or a command
                           on PATH, such as node. It receives the --verify-argument values, then the
                           publish directory and the published application's path. A nonzero exit
                           code fails the command.
  -h, --help               Show help
  --version                Show version
  --output <human|json>    Select output format

Examples:
  dotnet runic size --runtime linux-x64 --report measurements/linux.json

result.stdout:
Usage: dotnet runic support [options]

Preview, collect or remove a local support envelope built from an Editor diagnostic ZIP.

Options:
  --mode <mode>                preview lists what would be collected, collect writes the envelope,
                               and remove verifies and deletes it. [default: preview]
  --editor-diagnostics <editor-diagnostics>
                               The Editor diagnostic ZIP to read. Required by preview and collect.
  --destination <destination>  The support envelope JSON file. Required by collect and remove.
  -h, --help                   Show help
  --version                    Show version
  --output <human|json>        Select output format

Examples:
  dotnet runic support --mode preview --editor-diagnostics ./editor-diagnostics.zip
